subject.title: fix(agents): preserve runtime tool inheritance tokens

question: Should OpenClaw land this narrow runtime-selector inheritance fix after rebasing it onto current main, or fold the behavior into a broader subagent tool-policy/API change?
rationale: The patch changes an authorization boundary for spawned child sessions; tests can prove the mechanics, but maintainers must own whether this is the accepted boundary shape and how it should compose with the broader `toolsAllow` work.

options.title: Rebase And Land Narrow Fix
options.body: Resolve conflicts against current main, preserve the policy-filtered runtime selector helper, and land this PR as the focused fix for the MCP subagent inheritance bug.

options.title: Fold Into Broader Tool Work
options.body: Keep the canonical issue open and move this behavior into the broader `sessions_spawn.toolsAllow` or effective-tools visibility work if maintainers want one combined tool-policy change.

options.title: Pause For More Boundary Proof
options.body: Require additional maintainer-run or credentialed MCP proof before accepting any change that can expose runtime-materialized child tools.

recommendation.title: Rebase And Land Narrow Fix
recommendation.body: Resolve conflicts against current main, preserve the policy-filtered runtime selector helper, and land this PR as the focused fix for the MCP subagent inheritance bug.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main work changed the adjacent agent/Gateway tool-surface paths and the PR has already been pinged for maintainer review in that area.
